In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure and biological functions of plant lectins, and the present work is part of a larger project on the structure, function and evolution of plant lectins.
the isolation, characterization and crystallization of the bluebell (Scila campanulata), a mannose-specific plant lectin.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the structure of this lectin has been determined at a high resolution and that the structure of a mannose saccharide has been determined in the binding site of the protein, and the structure of the complex has been determined at 1.86 Angstroms resolution.
the crystal structure of the bluebell lectin has now been determined at a resolution of 2.0 A.
the bluebell mannose-binding lectins are a new class of plant lectins, which are distinct from other mannose-binding plant lectins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a mannose-binding protein (lectin) has been isolated from bluebell (S. campanulata), purified to homogeneity and crystallized.
we have crystallized a tetrameric mannose-specific lectins from Scilla campanulate bulbs, grown large crystals and determined the crystallographic structure.
we have crystallized the lectin and determined the crystallographic structure of a mannose binding lectin.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to grow crystals of a mannose binding lectin from blue bell (Scilla campaneulata) bulb in the presence of a mannose saccharide.
the lectin molecule is not a simple tetramer but is organized in an intricate way that is likely to be important for the function of the protein.
the bluebell lectin is an excellent model for the study of mannose-binding proteins.
